newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum shipments in April rise 5.8 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum shipments in April rise 5.8 percent.

text.p: Industry shipments of primary aluminum in the United States, including exports, in April were 5.8 percent above the same month in 1996, preliminary figures from the Aluminum Association indicated.
Actual shipments in April totaled 1.883 billion pounds or 854,115 tonnes, down 0.6 percent from March this year.
U.S. exports of aluminum ingot and mill products were reported at 290 million lbs in April, up 13.6 percent above the same month last year.
Imports totaling 620 million lbs, rose 5.8 percent over April 1996.
Domestic shipments in April, including imports but excluding exports, in April rose 4.5 percent to 1.593 billion lbs compared with April 1996.
Year to date domestic shipments rose 7.6 percent to 6.383 billion lbs.
However, in May the Association's order index fell 11.1 percent to 93.31 from 104.41 points in the previous month. Compared with May 1996, industry orders rose 7.28 points.
Domestic canstocks orders fell to 95.28 points in May compared to 109.63 in April, but were still above the 89.39 points in May 1996.
